hints: A height-n tower can be extended upward from a tower of height n-1 in one of two top configurations.
Track two counts: structures whose top blocks connect across both columns and structures whose top is split.
Derive each new pair of counts from the previous pair, then answer each test height from a precomputed table.
analogy: The top row can be in one of two shapes; each shape has a fixed set of ways to extend it.
example: For height 2 the recurrence gives 8 layouts; mirrored or rotated layouts remain distinct as the statement requires.
correctness: The top configuration uniquely determines which extension rule applies, and the recurrence counts every valid block arrangement with its orientation preserved.
complexity: O(maxQuery) preprocessing, O(1) per query, and O(maxQuery) memory.
algorithm: Let A[i] count layouts whose top has two separate vertical blocks and B[i] count layouts whose top is one joined shape. Initialize A[1]=B[1]=1; use A[i]=2*A[i-1]+B[i-1] and B[i]=A[i-1]+4*B[i-1], modulo 1,000,000,007. Answer A[n]+B[n].
